name: DNA methyltransferase 3 alpha

function.text: DNMT3A encodes a de novo DNA methyltransferase that establishes cytosine methylation patterns and helps regulate chromatin state, gene expression, and cellular differentiation.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to Tatton-Brown-Rahman overgrowth syndrome (autosomal dominant); Heyn-Sproul-Jackson syndrome (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Reported somatic alteration contexts include Acute myeloid leukemia; Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS; Nodal T-follicular helper cell lymphoma. The alteration class and exact variant must be assessed in the disease context.

function.text: DNMT3A encodes a DNA methyltransferase involved in establishing new DNA-methylation patterns, rather than simply copying an existing pattern after DNA replication. Methylation of CpG sites is an epigenetic modification important in development, genomic imprinting, and X-chromosome inactivation. DNMT3A expression is developmentally regulated, linking its role in DNA modification to changes in cellular state during development.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Tatton-Brown-Rahman overgrowth syndrome (autosomal dominant); Heyn-Sproul-Jackson syndrome (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving DNMT3A have been reported in acute myeloid leukemia, myelodysplastic syndromes, and peripheral t-cell lymphoma, NOS.
